title: Karnataka Courts Western India's Travel Market at TTF Mumbai as Domestic Tourism Hits Record Stride
excerpt: India's oldest travel trade fair drew over 10,000 professionals and 500 exhibitors to Mumbai, with Karnataka pitching heritage, wildlife and wellness tourism ahead of the festive season.
body:
• TTF Mumbai 2026, held August 20–22 at the Jio World Convention Centre, recorded a 35 percent increase in Day 1 trade visitors compared to the previous edition, with over 10,000 professionals attending.
  • Karnataka participated as a Partner State alongside Rajasthan, Kerala, Jammu & Kashmir and Madhya Pradesh, showcasing heritage sites like Hampi, wildlife sanctuaries, coastal destinations and wellness tourism circuits.
  • India recorded 4.3 billion domestic tourist visits in 2025, while 32.83 million Indian nationals traveled abroad — a 6.3 percent year-on-year increase — signaling sustained momentum in the travel sector.
  • The fair is timed to the industry's biggest buying window ahead of Diwali, the wedding season and winter holidays, when tour operators finalize inventories and partnerships.

India's Oldest Travel Fair Draws Record Numbers

TTF Mumbai 2026, India's oldest and largest travel trade exhibition, opened at the Jio World Convention Centre on August 20 to its strongest turnout in years. The three-day event, organized by Fairfest Media Limited, brought together more than 500 exhibitors, 20 Indian states and union territories, and participants from five countries in what serves as a premier B2B marketplace for the country's booming domestic travel industry.

Day 1 alone saw a 35 percent jump in trade visitor registrations compared to the previous edition, according to organizers. The Travel & Tourism Fair series, running since 1989, has positioned its Mumbai edition as the fastest-growing in the circuit, providing direct access to Maharashtra and Western India — the country's most valuable source market for leisure, corporate, MICE and outbound travel.

The timing is strategic. Indian tour operators use the August-September window to lock in partnerships and inventory ahead of the year's peak travel period: Diwali in October, the wedding season that follows, and winter holiday bookings through to March. TTF Mumbai follows Fairfest's OTM exhibition, held at the same venue in February, which was voted the leading travel trade show in Asia by NielsenIQ.

Karnataka's Tourism Push

Karnataka anchored a significant presence at the fair as one of five Partner States — alongside Rajasthan, Kerala, Jammu & Kashmir and Madhya Pradesh — while West Bengal, Delhi and Sikkim participated as Feature States. The state tourism board's pavilion focused on heritage destinations including Hampi's Stone Chariot and the Hoysaleshvara Temple, as well as wildlife, coastal, wellness and MICE tourism circuits.

The state's pitch targets Mumbai and Maharashtra specifically, recognizing the region as a major source market for Karnataka-bound travelers. Officials engaged with travel agents, tour operators, corporate planners and destination management companies across the three days, sharing promotional material and destination briefings on Karnataka's varied tourism circuits.

Karnataka has been expanding its tourism infrastructure beyond its established Bengaluru-Mysuru-Hampi corridor. The Yana Caves in Uttara Kannada, coffee plantation circuits in Chikmagalur, and coastal stretches along the Konkan coast are being promoted as alternatives for travelers increasingly seeking offbeat destinations.

Domestic Travel Boom Shapes the Landscape

The scale of TTF Mumbai reflects broader momentum in India's travel sector. The country recorded 4.3 billion domestic tourist visits in 2025, cementing its position as one of the world's largest domestic travel markets. Meanwhile, 32.83 million Indian nationals traveled abroad, registering a 6.3 percent year-on-year increase, according to industry data shared at the fair.

"The travel trade is witnessing strong momentum in domestic and Far East markets, with changing global dynamics and visa challenges for EU and US influencing traveller preferences. Travellers are increasingly seeking offbeat and lesser-known destinations."

— Rajesh Poddar, Chairman, Western Region, Travel Agents Association of India

The shift in travel patterns is notable. Visa difficulties for the European Union and the United States are redirecting Indian outbound traffic toward Southeast Asia, Japan, and Central Asian destinations that offer easier or visa-free access. Within India, the trend toward experiential and heritage tourism over conventional leisure trips is driving demand for states like Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and the northeastern states.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs planning trips to India during the festive and winter season, the TTF data points to growing infrastructure and package availability across destinations that were once hard to access without local planning. Karnataka's wellness tourism push, which includes Ayurvedic retreats and spa circuits, is specifically targeting the diaspora and international wellness traveler segment.

The broader trend of Indian states competing aggressively for both domestic and inbound tourists is also driving improvements in hospitality infrastructure, road connectivity and destination management — changes that benefit returning diaspora travelers as much as domestic tourists. With the festive booking window now open, the partnerships sealed at TTF Mumbai will determine which destinations and experiences dominate India's travel landscape through early 2027.
